seoTitle: How to Find Your Airtable Base ID
metaDescription: Locate your Airtable Base ID from the browser URL or from Airtable's own API documentation, and tell it apart from the table and view IDs that sit right next to it.
intro: Almost every integration that talks to Airtable, a Zapier automation, a custom script, a no-code app builder, asks for a Base ID before it can read or write your records. It's easy to find once you know where to look: your browser's address bar, or Airtable's auto-generated API documentation. This guide covers both, plus how to avoid grabbing the wrong ID when several look similar in the same URL.

steps.heading: Open the base you need the ID for
steps.body: From Airtable's Home screen, click into the specific base. Every base has its own distinct ID, so opening the wrong one and copying its ID will point an integration at the wrong data. Home lists each base with the workspace it belongs to, which helps if you manage several bases across different teams.

image.caption: Airtable's Home screen. Open the exact base you need the ID for, since each base has its own identifier.

steps.heading: Read the ID from the URL
steps.body: With the base open, look at the address bar. The Base ID is the segment that starts with "app" and runs up to the next forward slash, for example appeqX9XTkHZNfSbn in https://airtable.com/appeqX9XTkHZNfSbn/pagIk60ZUF9P5UP72/. It's the fastest of the two methods, but the same URL also carries a table ID and sometimes a view ID right next to it, so it's worth knowing what each prefix means before copying.

steps.heading: Or confirm it through the API documentation
steps.body: Click the Help icon in the upper right of any screen and choose API documentation. Airtable generates this reference per account, and the page dynamically shows the Base ID for whichever base you were just working in, alongside the base's name. This is a useful second check when a URL you copied looks off, since the API docs display the ID plainly rather than buried in a path.

image.caption: The Help menu, with API documentation listed. This opens Airtable's developer reference for the account.

steps.heading: Find and open your base in the reference
steps.body: The API Reference opens on an introduction describing the Airtable API in general. Scroll down and it lists every workspace and base in the account as a clickable card. Click the card for the base you need; that opens documentation scoped to just that base, with its Base ID shown at the top, ready to copy.

image.caption: The API Reference introduction, listing bases by workspace. Clicking a card opens documentation for that base, with its Base ID at the top.

steps.heading: Store it with the right credential
steps.body: A Base ID on its own isn't a secret; it identifies which base to talk to but doesn't grant access. The personal access token or API key is what determines whether a request carrying that ID is allowed to read or write anything. Keep both together in your integration's environment variables or secrets manager, and avoid pasting either into shared documents or public code.

faq.question: What does an Airtable Base ID look like?
faq.answer: An alphanumeric string starting with "app", such as appeqX9XTkHZNfSbn. Table IDs start with "tbl" and view IDs with "viw", so the prefix is what tells them apart.

faq.question: Is my Base ID sensitive information I need to hide?
faq.answer: No. It identifies a base but doesn't grant access on its own. The credential worth protecting is your API key or personal access token, since that's what actually authorizes requests.

faq.question: Can I find the Base ID without opening the API documentation?
faq.answer: Yes, it's visible directly in the browser's address bar whenever the base is open. Look for the segment starting with "app".

faq.question: Why does the API documentation list all my bases instead of just one?
faq.answer: Airtable generates a documentation page per base, so the introduction page groups every base you have access to by workspace. You click through to the one you need.

faq.question: I copied an ID starting with 'tbl' by mistake. What is that?
faq.answer: That's a Table ID, not a Base ID. It sits in the URL right after the Base ID, which is the usual reason the two get mixed up.

verifiedNote: Click path and screens come from a recorded walkthrough. The ID formats, the Help-menu route to the API documentation, and the table/view/record ID prefixes were checked against Airtable's own support documentation in September 2026; no factual corrections were needed, so this pass mainly tightened the steps and added the prefix reference table.
